newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telebras leads Latin ADRs in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telebras leads Latin ADRs in New York.

text.p: Brazilian telecom Telebras rebounded on Tuesday to lead Latin American stocks, and Sweden's LM Ericsson was hit by reaction to its earnings, traders said.
Most Latin American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) followed the New York markets, which rallied after the October index of U.S. consumer confidence came in weaker than expected.
"Every time the Dow (Jones Industrial Average) goes up 20 points, we go up. Every time the Dow goes down, we go down," said Lucia Skwarek, head of Latin American equities trading for UBS Securities.

Telebras, Brazil's state-run telephone company, was up 2-3/4 to 73-1/4 in late-morning trade. The rise followed Morgan Stanley's announcement it had raised its forecast for the company's earnings per ADR to $8.18 from $7.75 this year and to $9.65 from $9.46 in 1997.

Telebras has been weighed down by worries about a court decision last week that supported a company subscription of shares in 1990. Brazil shares also have been weakened by the country's trade deficit.
Both Morgan Stanley and Oppenheimer & Co maintained their buy recommendations on the stock.

"We believe that the market has oversold Telebras shares, correcting 11.9 percent versus 5.9 percent for the market over the past seven days," analysts Jose Linares and Stefanie Mollin said in a report.
Argentine stocks strengthened as investors shrugged off political worries. Telecom Argentina was up 1/4 to 37-3/8 and Telefonica de Argentina rose 1/8 to 23.

Ericsson was off 14/16 to 27-5/16 after the company reported a 30 percent increase in nine-month profits. Traders said the fall came because the increase was slightly below that expected by New York analysts.
Australia's News Corp was off 1/8 to 22-3/8 following news it had named Peter Chernin president and chief operating officer and created an office-of-the-chairman management structure.

Andrew Melinek, head of ADR research and sales at NatWest Securities, said that despite the stock's dip the changes were welcome. "We perceive it to be good news in line with the consolidation they've been talking about," he said.

Drug stocks were weighed by concerns that the likely re-election of President Bill Clinton next week could lead to a revival of plans for national health insurance. Britain's SmithKline Beecham Plc was off 3/4 to 61-3/8.
Declining stocks led advancing shares by a margin of 168 to 85 in a selected 441-ADR index.
